n: Once everyone has crossed, the Lord gives Joshua a new instruction. Miracles are meant to be remembered.
Choose twelve men, one from each tribe — every tribe shares in the memorial.

f.w: out of every tribe a man

n: Each man takes a stone from the exact spot where the priests stood in the riverbed and carries it to that night’s campsite.
Joshua summons the twelve men already chosen.

f.g: Whom he had appointed in advance.

n: Each man returns into the riverbed, past the ark, and hoists a stone on his shoulder.
The stones are meant to spark questions from children. Memorials invite family teaching.

f.w: when your children ask their fathers

n: Parents will answer: the river stopped before the ark of the Lord. The stones bear lasting witness. Latter-day Saints use journals, sacrament, and temples similarly as reminders.
The twelve men do exactly as commanded and lay the stones down at the camp.

f.w: as the LORD spake unto Joshua

n: Joshua also sets up a second circle of twelve stones in the riverbed where the priests stood — visible “unto this day” to the writer’s readers, perhaps at low water.

f.g: A phrase showing the account was written down some time after the events.

n: The priests held their place in midriver until everything was done, while the people hurried across.
Last of all, the ark and priests crossed in full view of the people.

f.w: in the presence of the people

n: The eastern tribes kept their promise to Moses, crossing armed ahead of the others.
About 40,000 warriors crossed to the plains of Jericho, ready for battle “before the Lord.”

f.g: In God’s presence, as his army.

n: God fulfilled his promise: Joshua was honored before Israel, who now respected him as they had Moses.
The Lord speaks again to Joshua.

f.g: Joshua acts only on God’s word.

n: Command the priests carrying the ark to come up out of the river.

f.g: So called because it held the tablets of the covenant (the “testimony”).

n: Joshua relays the command.

f.g: Climb up out of the riverbed.

n: The moment the priests’ feet touched dry land, the waters rushed back to flood level — proof that the river had been held back by God.

f.w: the waters of Jordan returned unto their place

n: The date: the 10th day of the first month — the very day Passover lambs were chosen. Exactly forty years after leaving Egypt, Israel camps at Gilgal.

f.w: the tenth day of the first month

f.g: Probably “circle” (of stones); Israel’s base camp near Jericho.

n: Joshua sets up the twelve stones at Gilgal.
He repeats the instruction: when children ask about the stones…
…tell them: Israel crossed this river on dry ground.
God dried up the Jordan just as he did the Red Sea. The two crossings bracket the wilderness era.

f.w: as the LORD your God did to the Red sea

n: Two purposes: that the whole world will know God’s power, and that Israel will reverence him forever.

f.w: That all the people of the earth might know
the hand of the LORD, that it is mighty
